findings.message: slide 5 ('Reliability Metrics: MTBF, MTTR, Availability, SLOs'): [fact] The availability formula is presented without noting that it assumes comparable measurement intervals and a steady-state system, and it can be confused with the percentage form of availability. Fix: State the assumptions and show the equivalent percentage formula, Availability = MTBF/(MTBF + MTTR) × 100%.

findings.message: slide 7 ('Scenario 1: Microservice Deployment Evaluation'): [fact] The stated outcome that the error budget is exhausted is not derivable from the supplied latency and error-rate metrics because no SLO window, request volume, or burn-rate data are given. Fix: Either provide the observation window and request volume needed to calculate the burn rate, or phrase the outcome as an SLO breach with error-budget status to be evaluated.

slide 8 ('Scenario 2: AI Model Serving Pipeline Evaluation'): [fact] The SLO is described as a drift score below 0.1 without defining the drift metric, its scale, or direction, so the threshold cannot be evaluated reliably. Fix: Name the drift metric and scale, for example PSI, and state the threshold and alert direction explicitly.

findings.message: slide 8 ('Scenario 2: AI Model Serving Pipeline Evaluation'): [fact] The notes claim that preprocessing takes 600ms and that horizontal scaling and model batching are demonstrated, but the slide provides no supporting measurements or batching details. findings.message: slide 12 ('Hands-On: Instrument and Evaluate a Sample Project'): [other] The activity requires students to clone a repository and deploy to local Kubernetes, but no repository URL, setup instructions, prerequisites, or fallback for environments without Kubernetes are provided. findings.message: slide 13 ('Check: Metric Selection for AI Model Serving'): [quiz] The question asks for the most critical metric for detecting real-time model-serving performance degradation, but CPU utilization can also reveal resource-related degradation and the question does not specify the failure mode. Fix: Ask which metric directly measures real-time tail-latency degradation, or specify that the concern is user-facing request performance.

evidence.title: Check: Metric Selection for AI Model Serving

findings.message: slide 14 ('Check: Reliability Evaluation Decision'): [quiz] A burn rate above 10x does not uniquely determine the automated action because the correct response depends on the configured burn-rate policy and the remaining error budget.
